title: Provider-rejected embed payloads poison their batch and strand items through every backfill
wanted_capability: Per-item poison handling in the embed queue. Surfaced 2026-06-13 by the new backfill/stall visibility (gap-b9d39c10 follow-on): the code route's last ~0.7% residue (595 items) turns out to be payloads Voyage rejects with HTTP 400 ("request body is not valid JSON, or some arguments were not specified properly") — the whole 52-item batch drops after 3 retries, taking innocent items with it, the route flips unavailable, and the same items re-fail every nightly backfill (bounded churn, never converges). Wanted: (a) on a 4xx batch rejection, bisect/retry per-item so one bad payload doesn't drop 51 good ones; (b) persist a poison list (entity_id+chunk_hash) that enqueue skips and bbox_embed_status reports as a distinct count, so coverage can honestly converge to "1.0 minus N poisoned"; (c) diagnose the actual payload defect (likely oversized chunk or content the request builder mis-serializes) and sanitize/split at chunk time.
fallback_used: None needed immediately — route availability recovers on the next successful batch; the 595 items stay unembedded and re-churn nightly.
evidence: bbox_embed_status 2026-06-13: code available=false retried_count=6 last_error=HTTP 400 batch_size=52
code coverage plateau 0.9933 (87603/88198) across manual refill + backfill
resolution_note: Root cause confirmed by a live Voyage probe: empty-string chunks → HTTP 400 "Input cannot contain empty strings", and the rejection dropped the whole 52-item batch after 3 identical retries (51 good batch-mates stranded, route flipped unavailable, re-failed every nightly backfill). Fix (commit 857206b0, worktree storage-maintenance-leaks): (a) empty/whitespace text skipped at enqueue AND excluded from coverage via shared embeddable_text predicate — the direct fix; (b) payload-level HTTP 4xx (not 408/429) classified NonRetryableBatchError by the Voyage provider, and the queue worker bisects such a batch to the poison item(s) instead of retry-then-drop, so one bad payload can't strand batch-mates (call budget bounds the pass); (c) durable dropped_count + last_dropped on RouteStatus that mark_success does NOT clear (the original last_error overloading was why the test caught the good batch-mate clobbering the drop record); poison isolation keeps the route available; (d) bbox_embed_status stall reason distinguishes poison from un-enqueued residue so operators aren't pointed at a backfill that can't help. Full suite 3,966 green. NOT done from the gap's wishlist: a persisted cross-restart poison skip-list (current design re-bisects poison each backfill — cheap since empty-text is now skipped pre-enqueue, so the residual poison set is tiny/empty in practice) and chunk-time sanitization of the underlying defect. Pending: merge to beta + deploy (in progress this session).
